title: UCSB AI Services Benchmark
text:
A systematic evaluation of large language models available through UCSB-managed AI infrastructure —
    comparing performance, speed, and capability across on-premise and cloud-hosted services.
summary  = FileAttachment("data/results_summary.csv").csv({ typed: true })
lb       = FileAttachment("data/leaderboard.json").json()
families = FileAttachment("data/model_families.json").json()
n_models    = new Set(lb.map(d => d.model)).size
n_services  = new Set(lb.map(d => d.service)).size
n_tests     = 12 + 12 + 6   // v1 + v2 + multimodal
n_evals     = 345

title: UCSB AI Services Benchmark
text:
Infrastructure

  Three UCSB-managed services were benchmarked, spanning two infrastructure models:
  on-premise Ollama clusters and cloud-hosted Amazon Bedrock.




  
    GRIT
    🖥️ On-premise · Ollama
    llm.grit.ucsb.edu
    
      UCSB's General Research IT cluster. Models are served locally via Ollama on
      UCSB-managed hardware. Largest model catalog — 14 models evaluated including
      vision-capable models.
    
    14 models evaluated  ·  Budget: 10M tokens/month
  

  
    CIT
    🖥️ On-premise · Ollama
    api.ai.college.ucsb.edu
    
      College of Information Technology servers. Also Ollama-based, but shows notably
      higher throughput than GRIT for the same models — reflecting different hardware capacity.
      6 models evaluated.
    
    6 models evaluated  ·  Budget: 10M tokens/month
  

  
    AICommons
    ☁️ Cloud · Amazon Bedrock
    zkh52rh785.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
    
      AWS-hosted API with a diverse catalog including Claude, GPT-4o, Amazon Nova, and
      Llama 4. Currently 1 model evaluated (gpt-4o). Additional evaluations planned.
    
    1 model evaluated  ·  Budget: 900K tokens/month

Acknowledgements

  🙏 DreamLab — Acknowledgement
  
    The UCSB DreamLab (litellm.dreamlab.ucsb.edu) also participated in this evaluation project,
    providing access to Google Gemini models (gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.1-pro-preview,
    and others) via a LiteLLM proxy. DreamLab models were used extensively as the default LLM judge
    during iterative development of this benchmark suite.
    DreamLab results are not included in the comparative dashboard because DreamLab
    cannot guarantee the continued availability of LLM inference services going forward.
    We thank the DreamLab team for their support of this work and their contribution to
    UCSB's AI research infrastructure.
